messages:
laura_nimbus: Hey team — we rotated IdP certs at ~2026-03-14 02:00 UTC and pushed new metadata. Since then some users at NimbusPay can't SSO: ~30% of logins fail with 'Invalid SAML Assertion: Audience URI mismatch' and others get 'Recipient mismatch'. Errors are intermittent (some users succeed, some fail). We included the SAMLResponse base64 in the support ticket (I'll paste if you need). Metadata URL: https://idp.nimbuspay.example/.well-known/saml/metadata.xml. Can you advise?

sara_support: thanks for the report — sorry about the interruption. a few quick asks so we can triage fast: 1) can you paste one failing SAMLResponse (base64) here or DM it to me? 2) what's the SP entityID & ACS URL you expect us to see (include trailing slash if any)? 3) can you try login with ?saml_debug=1 and attach the IdP debug dump if available? 4) did you change metadata URL or any proxy in front of the IdP? any CDN?

laura_nimbus: I pasted a base64 blob into the ticket (ticket #SUP-8892). Our SP entityID is https://app.redwood.example/saml/metadata and ACS is https://app.redwood.example/saml/acs (no trailing slash normally). We do sit behind FastEdge CDN for the IdP metadata (TTL 10m). We did not change the ACS.

ben_sso: joining — can you give me one of the failing SAMLResponse blobs? i'll decode quickly. command I use:

```
# decode and pretty print
echo "<BASE64>" | base64 -d | xmllint --format - 2>/dev/null | sed -n '1,200p'
```

ben_sso: decoded one of the failing responses and saw two suspicious things: 1) <Audience> element is `https://app.redwood.example/saml/metadata/` (note trailing slash) while your SP entityID is without slash -> audience mismatch. 2) The <SubjectConfirmationData Recipient="https://app.redwood.example/saml/acs/" .../> contains a trailing slash. So some component is rewriting URLs to add a trailing slash. here's an excerpt (sanitized):

```
<saml:Assertion ...>
  <saml:Conditions>
    <saml:AudienceRestriction>
      <saml:Audience>https://app.redwood.example/saml/metadata/</saml:Audience>
    </saml:AudienceRestriction>
  </saml:Conditions>
  <saml:Subject>
    <saml:SubjectConfirmation>
      <saml:SubjectConfirmationData Recipient="https://app.redwood.example/saml/acs/" NotOnOrAfter="2026-03-14T02:03:12Z"/>
    </saml:SubjectConfirmation>
  </saml:Subject>
</saml:Assertion>
```

ben_sso: that explains the Audience/Recipient mismatch errors. we should check what rewrites the metadata — my guess: the CDN/proxy in front of the IdP metadata is normalizing paths and adding slashes. also saw the IdP metadata contains two KeyDescriptor entries (old cert + new cert) but the order changed during rotation and our metadata-proxy cached the older ordering for some requests. that may explain intermittent failures (some requests hit a cached metadata copy referencing the old cert).

incidents-bot: Automated alert: metadata-cache-miss triggered for customer=nimbuspay at 2026-03-14T02:07:11Z — fallback to cached metadata.

olivia_sre: i'm on the call. olivia_sre here — i've checked our metadata-proxy logs: between 02:05–02:06 we returned cached metadata for ~40% of requests with stale cache-control headers (edge TTL not honored due to a bug). that matches the timing. also saw a header rewrite that adds a trailing slash if the path lacks an extension. i'll open a blocker ticket on infra.

sara_support: proposed immediate triage steps: 1) laura, can you temporarily republish your IdP metadata with both ACS & EntityID aliases: include both with and without trailing slash (add Audience/Recipient variants) — this is the fastest customer-side workaround. 2) we'll flush our metadata-proxy caches for your customer id. olivia, can you run a manual cache invalidation and confirm? 3) ben, can we accept both trailing slash variants in SP validation as a temporary relax? if not, can we give a clear roll-forward plan?

ben_sso: i can put a short lived permissive check in place to accept trailing slash variants for the next 24 hours while we fix proxy. code snippet to decode/check locally:

```
# check audience and recipient quickly
AUD="https://app.redwood.example/saml/metadata"
REC="https://app.redwood.example/saml/acs"
# compare normalized
normalized_aud=$(echo "$EXTRACTED_AUD" | sed 's:/$::')
normalized_rec=$(echo "$EXTRACTED_REC" | sed 's:/$::')
if [ "$normalized_aud" = "$AUD" ] && [ "$normalized_rec" = "$REC" ]; then
  echo ok
fi
```

olivia_sre: cache invalidation done for customer=nimbuspay via /admin/metadata/flush?customer=nimbuspay — response: 200 OK. infra also pushed a temporary header rule to stop the path-normalization rewrite for .well-known and /saml/* metadata endpoints. i'll monitor for 30m.

laura_nimbus: after you flushed cache i just tested and a handful of users who were failing earlier can now login. seems promising. i'll keep monitoring and report any failures. thanks for the quick turn.

sara_support: next steps and owners: - ben_sso -> push permissive validation & unit test (temporary, revert after 24h) PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/4532 - olivia_sre -> root cause fix in metadata-proxy (preserve trailing slash semantics + respect cache-control) and roll out within 4 hours - laura_nimbus (customer) -> consider keeping both certs in IdP metadata for a 48h overlap window during rotation; republish with explicit aliases if possible - sara_support -> coordinate and keep this thread updated, will close when stable for 24h

ben_sso: i'll open the permissive validation PR now and tag @olivia_sre for a rollback reminder. ETA ~30m for the hotfix, full proxy patch will take longer.

olivia_sre: monitoring green so far, no new metadata-cache-miss alerts for nimbuspay. i'll keep an eye and post status update in ~1h.

laura_nimbus: thx everyone. will ping if anything else crops up. appreciate the help :pray:

sara_support: closing notes: root cause = metadata-proxy rewrite + stale cached metadata after cert rotation causing Audience/Recipient mismatch and intermittent key ordering. mitigations = cache flush + temporary permissive acceptor + proxy config change + customer-side overlap in cert metadata. owners listed above.
